tldr: NVIDIA opened its Nemotron 3 family further on Aug 11 with 3.5 Lightning and a companion NeMo Switchyard release, aimed at agentic workloads rather than chatbots. By Aug 17 the 30B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model (3B active) had its first managed-cloud distribution channel: AWS SageMaker JumpStart.
whats_new: TheSequence's Aug 19 frontier-model rundown groups Nemotron 3.5 Lightning with DeepSeek V4-Pro and GLM-5.3, two days after AWS added the 30B-MoE (3B-active) build to SageMaker JumpStart.
why_it_matters: A 30B MoE with only 3B active parameters plus SageMaker JumpStart availability gives platform teams a low-latency, open-weight option for agentic tool-calling without standing up custom serving infrastructure.

status.detail: Shipped by NVIDIA on Aug 11 and reached managed-cloud availability via AWS SageMaker JumpStart on Aug 17.

beats.headline: NVIDIA ships Nemotron 3.5 Lightning + NeMo Switchyard for agentic workloads
beats.summary: Expansion of the Nemotron 3 family, pitched at agent deployments over chat.

beats.headline: 30B-MoE (3B active) build lands in AWS SageMaker JumpStart
beats.summary: First managed-cloud deployment path outside NVIDIA's own channels.

beats.headline: TheSequence groups it with DeepSeek V4-Pro and GLM-5.3 in a frontier-model rundown

open_questions: What does NeMo Switchyard actually do — the Aug 11 announcement pairs it with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning but doesn't explain its role.
Will Nemotron 3.5 Lightning reach deployment surfaces beyond SageMaker JumpStart, such as NVIDIA NIM, Hugging Face, or other clouds?
take_for_builders: If you're benchmarking open-weight models for agent tool-calling, try Nemotron 3.5 Lightning via the SageMaker JumpStart path before committing to custom serving — its 3B-active/30B-total split targets that cost/latency profile.
